001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.lang.StackWalker.Option;
004import java.lang.StackWalker.StackFrame;
005import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
006import java.time.Instant;
007import java.util.List;
008import java.util.Locale;
009import java.util.Objects;
010
011import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
012
013import io.jstach.rainbowgum.KeyValues.MutableKeyValues;

015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent.Rewriter;

017
018/**
019 * A LogEvent is a container for a single call to a logger. An event should not be created
020 * unless a route or logger is actually enabled.
021 *
022 * @author agentgt
023 * @apiNote LogEvent is currently sealed. The reason there are so many static creation
024 * methods is for optimization purposes because other than actual outputting creating
025 * events is generally the most expensive operation (mostly in terms of memory) a logging
026 * system does.
027 * @see LogMessageFormatter
028 */
029public sealed interface LogEvent {
030
031        /**
032         * Creates a log event.
033         * @param timestamp time of event
034         * @param threadName or empty string
035         * @param threadId thread id or 0 if that cannot be resolved.
036         * @param level the logging level.
037         * @param loggerName the name of the logger which is usually a class name.
038         * @param formattedMessage the unformatted message.
039         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
040         * @param throwable an exception if passed maybe <code>null</code>.
041         * @return event
042         * @see LevelResolver
043         * @apiNote the message is already assumed to be formatted as no arguments are passed.
044         */
045        public static LogEvent of(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
046                        String loggerName, @Nullable String formattedMessage, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
047                return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, formattedMessage, keyValues,
048                                throwable);
049        }
050
051        /**
052         * Creates a log event.
053         * @param timestamp time of event
054         * @param threadName or empty string
055         * @param threadId thread id or 0 if that cannot be resolved.
056         * @param level the logging level.
057         * @param loggerName the name of the logger which is usually a class name.
058         * @param message the unformatted message.
059         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
060         * @param messageFormatter formatter to use for rendering a message when
061         * #{@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called.
062         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to messageFormatter. If it is a
063         * {@link Throwable} see
064         * {@link #ofAll(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable, LogMessageFormatter, Object[])}.
065         * @return event
066         * @see LevelResolver
067         * @see LogMessageFormatter
068         */
069        public static LogEvent ofOneArg(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
070                        String loggerName, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter,
071                        @Nullable Object arg1) {
072                var t = throwableInsteadOfArgument(messageFormatter, arg1);
073                if (t != null) {
074                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues, t);
075                }
076                var throwable = throwableAlsoArgument(messageFormatter, arg1);
077                if (message == null) {
078                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
079                                        throwable);
080
081                }
082                return new OneArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
083                                messageFormatter, throwable, arg1);
084        }
085
086        /**
087         * Creates a log event.
088         * @param timestamp time of event
089         * @param threadName or empty string
090         * @param threadId thread id or 0 if that cannot be resolved.
091         * @param level the logging level.
092         * @param loggerName the name of the logger which is usually a class name.
093         * @param message the unformatted message.
094         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
095         * @param messageFormatter formatter to use for rendering a message when
096         * #{@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called.
097         * @param arg1 argument that will be passed to messageFormatter.
098         * @param arg2 argument that will be passed to messageFormatter. If it is a
099         * {@link Throwable} see
100         * {@link #ofAll(Instant, String, long, Level, String, String, KeyValues, Throwable, LogMessageFormatter, Object[])}.
101         * @return event
102         * @see LevelResolver
103         * @see LogMessageFormatter
104         */
105        public static LogEvent ofTwoArgs(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
106                        String loggerName, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter,
107                        @Nullable Object arg1, @Nullable Object arg2) {
108                var t = throwableInsteadOfArgument(messageFormatter, arg2);
109                if (t != null) {
110                        if (message == null) {
111                                return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues, t);
112                        }
113                        return new OneArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
114                                        messageFormatter, t, arg1);
115                }
116                var throwable = throwableAlsoArgument(messageFormatter, arg2);
117                if (message == null) {
118                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
119                                        throwable);
120                }
121                return new TwoArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
122                                messageFormatter, throwable, arg1, arg2);
123        }
124
125        /**
126         * Creates a log event with everything specified.
127         * @param timestamp time of event
128         * @param threadName or empty string
129         * @param threadId thread id or 0 if that cannot be resolved.
130         * @param level the logging level.
131         * @param loggerName the name of the logger which is usually a class name.
132         * @param message the unformatted message.
133         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
134         * @param throwable or <code>null</code>.
135         * @param messageFormatter formatter to use for rendering a message when
136         * #{@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called.
137         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to messageFormatter. The
138         * contents maybe null elements but the array itself should not be null. If throwable
139         * is null and the last argument is a {@link Throwable}: with
140         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#SLF4J} it is the event's
141         * throwable instead of an argument; with
142         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#JUL} it is an argument; with
143         * {@link LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)} it is an argument, and also the
144         * event's throwable when {@value LogProperties#MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY} is
145         * <code>log4j2</code>.
146         * @return event
147         * @see LevelResolver
148         * @see LogMessageFormatter
149         */
150        public static LogEvent ofAll(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
151                        String loggerName, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Throwable throwable,
152                        LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter, @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable List<@Nullable Object> args) {
153
154                if (args == null) {
155                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
156                                        throwable);
157                }
158                int length = args.size();
159                if (throwable == null && length > 0) {
160                        var last = args.get(length - 1);
161                        var t = throwableInsteadOfArgument(messageFormatter, last);
162                        if (t != null) {
163                                throwable = t;
164                                length = length - 1;
165                        }
166                        else {
167                                throwable = throwableAlsoArgument(messageFormatter, last);
168                        }
169                }
170                if (message == null) {
171                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
172                                        throwable);
173                }
174
175                return switch (length) {
176                        case 0 ->
177                                new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues, throwable);
178                        case 1 -> new OneArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
179                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args.get(0));
180                        case 2 -> new TwoArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
181                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args.get(0), args.get(1));
182                        default -> new ArrayArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
183                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args.toArray(), length);
184                };
185        }
186
187        /**
188         * Creates a log event with everything specified.
189         * @param timestamp time of event
190         * @param threadName or empty string
191         * @param threadId thread id or 0 if that cannot be resolved.
192         * @param level the logging level.
193         * @param loggerName the name of the logger which is usually a class name.
194         * @param message the unformatted message.
195         * @param keyValues key values that come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
196         * @param throwable or <code>null</code>.
197         * @param messageFormatter formatter to use for rendering a message when
198         * #{@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)} is called.
199         * @param args an array of arguments that will be passed to messageFormatter. The
200         * contents maybe null elements but the array itself should not be null. If throwable
201         * is null and the last argument is a {@link Throwable}: with
202         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#SLF4J} it is the event's
203         * throwable instead of an argument; with
204         * {@link LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter#JUL} it is an argument; with
205         * {@link LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)} it is an argument, and also the
206         * event's throwable when {@value LogProperties#MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY} is
207         * <code>log4j2</code>.
208         * @return event
209         * @see LevelResolver
210         * @see LogMessageFormatter
211         */
212        public static LogEvent ofAll(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
213                        String loggerName, @Nullable String message, KeyValues keyValues, @Nullable Throwable throwable,
214                        LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter, @SuppressWarnings("exports") @Nullable Object @Nullable [] args) {
215
216                if (args == null) {
217                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
218                                        throwable);
219                }
220                int length = args.length;
221                if (throwable == null && length > 0) {
222                        var last = args[length - 1];
223                        var t = throwableInsteadOfArgument(messageFormatter, last);
224                        if (t != null) {
225                                throwable = t;
226                                length = length - 1;
227                        }
228                        else {
229                                throwable = throwableAlsoArgument(messageFormatter, last);
230                        }
231                }
232                if (message == null) {
233                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
234                                        throwable);
235                }
236
237                return switch (length) {
238                        case 0 ->
239                                new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues, throwable);
240                        case 1 -> new OneArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
241                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args[0]);
242                        case 2 -> new TwoArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
243                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args[0], args[1]);
244                        default -> new ArrayArgLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, keyValues,
245                                        messageFormatter, throwable, args, length);
246                };
247        }
248
249        /*
250         * SLF4J treats a trailing Throwable argument as the event's throwable instead of an
251         * argument.
252         */
253        private static @Nullable Throwable throwableInsteadOfArgument(LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter,
254                        @Nullable Object arg) {
255                if (messageFormatter == LogMessageFormatter.StandardMessageFormatter.SLF4J && arg instanceof Throwable t) {
256                        return t;
257                }
258                return null;
259        }
260
261        /*
262         * The java.util.logging and System.Logger MessageFormat style formats a trailing
263         * Throwable argument like any other argument, as the JDK, the jul-to-slf4j bridge and
264         * JBoss Logging do. With the log4j2 style it is also the event's throwable, as
265         * Log4j2's MessageFormatMessage does, so the message is complete and the stack trace
266         * is logged.
267         */
268        private static @Nullable Throwable throwableAlsoArgument(LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter,
269                        @Nullable Object arg) {
270                if (arg instanceof Throwable t && MessageFormatStyle.throwableAlsoArgument(messageFormatter)) {
271                        return t;
272                }
273                return null;
274        }
275
276        /**
277         * Creates a new event with the caller info attached. <em> This method always returns
278         * a new event does not check if the original has caller info. </em>
279         * @param event original event.
280         * @param caller caller info.
281         * @return new log event.
282         */
283        public static LogEvent withCaller(LogEvent event, Caller caller) {
284                return new StackFrameLogEvent(event, caller);
285        }
286
287        /**
288         * Creates an event that is the given event at a different level. Nothing checks
289         * whether the new level is enabled; a route drops an event its
290         * {@linkplain LogRouter.Router.Filter filters} moved to a level it does not enable.
291         * @param event original event.
292         * @param level level of the returned event.
293         * @return the given event if it already has the level, otherwise an event with the
294         * level.
295         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the level is {@link Level#ALL} or
296         * {@link Level#OFF}.
297         */
298        public static LogEvent withLevel(LogEvent event, Level level) {
299                if (level == Level.ALL || level == Level.OFF) {
300                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("An event cannot have level " + level + ".");
301                }
302                if (event.level() == level) {
303                        return event;
304                }
305                if (event instanceof LevelLogEvent e) {
306                        var original = e.event();
307                        return original.level() == level ? original : new LevelLogEvent(original, level);
308                }
309                return new LevelLogEvent(event, level);
310        }
311
312        /**
313         * Creates an event whose message, message presence, key values or throwable come from
314         * the rewriter. Everything else is the given event's.
315         * @param event original event.
316         * @param rewriter rewrites parts of the event.
317         * @return rewritten event.
318         * @see #withLevel(LogEvent, Level)
319         */
320        public static LogEvent rewrite(LogEvent event, Rewriter rewriter) {
321                return new RewrittenLogEvent(event, rewriter);
322        }
323
324        /**
325         * Timestamp when the event was created.
326         * @return instant when the event was created.
327         */
328        public Instant timestamp();
329
330        /**
331         * Name of the thread.
332         * @return thread name.
333         * @apiNote this maybe empty and often is if virtual threads are used.
334         */
335        public String threadName();
336
337        /**
338         * Thread id.
339         * @return thread id.
340         */
341        public long threadId();
342
343        /**
344         * The logging level. {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level#ALL} and
345         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level#OFF} should not be returned as they have
346         * special meaning.
347         * @return level.
348         */
349        public System.Logger.Level level();
350
351        /**
352         * Name of logger.
353         * @return name of logger.
354         */
355        public String loggerName();
356
357        /**
358         * Unformatted message, before arguments are filled in, including after the event is
359         * {@linkplain #freeze() frozen}. A {@linkplain #rewrite(LogEvent, Rewriter) rewritten
360         * event} has no arguments, so its message is the rewritten message.
361         * @return unformatted message
362         * @see #formattedMessage(StringBuilder)
363         */
364        public String message();
365
366        /**
367         * {@link #message()} or <code>null</code> if the event has no message.
368         * @return message or <code>null</code>.
369         * @see #formattedMessage(StringBuilder)
370         */
371        default @Nullable String messageOrNull() {
372                if (hasMessage()) {
373                        return message();
374                }
375                return null;
376        }
377
378        /**
379         * If the event has a message or not. Because the return of {@link #message()} is non
380         * null there is no way to detect that a message is missing.
381         * @return <code>true</code> if this event has a message.
382         */
383        default public boolean hasMessage() {
384                return true;
385        }
386
387        /**
388         * Appends the formatted message.
389         * @param sb string builder to use.
390         * @see LogMessageFormatter
391         */
392        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb);
393
394        /**
395         * Appends the formatted message.
396         * @param sb string builder to use.
397         * @param fallbackMessage string to use if the message was never set.
398         * @see LogMessageFormatter
399         * @see #hasMessage()
400         */
401        default void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb, String fallbackMessage) {
402                if (hasMessage()) {
403                        formattedMessage(sb);
404                }
405                else {
406                        sb.append(fallbackMessage);
407                }
408        }
409
410        /**
411         * Throwable at the time of the event passed from the logger.
412         * @return if the event does not have a throwable <code>null</code> will be returned.
413         */
414        public @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull();
415
416        /**
417         * Key values that usually come from MDC or an SLF4J Event Builder.
418         * @return key values.
419         */
420        public KeyValues keyValues();
421
422        /**
423         * Returns info about caller or <code>null</code> if not supported.
424         * @return caller info
425         */
426        default @Nullable Caller callerOrNull() {
427                return null;
428        }
429
430        /**
431         * Freeze will return a LogEvent that is safe to use in a different thread. Usually
432         * this entails copying the data or checking if it is already immutable. Freeze should
433         * be called before passing an event to an {@link LogPublisher.AsyncLogPublisher}.
434         * @return thread safe log event.
435         */
436        public LogEvent freeze();
437
438        /**
439         * Freeze and replace with the given timestamp.
440         * @param timestamp instant to replace timestamp in this.
441         * @return a copy of this with the given timestamp.
442         */
443        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp);
444
445        /**
446         * Caller info usually derived from Stack walking.
447         */
448        public sealed interface Caller {
449
450                /**
451                 * Creates caller info from a stack frame.
452                 * @param stackFrame stack frame must have
453                 * {@link java.lang.StackWalker.Option#RETAIN_CLASS_REFERENCE}.
454                 * @return caller info.
455                 */
456                public static Caller of(StackFrame stackFrame) {
457                        return new StackFrameCallerInfo(stackFrame);
458                }
459
460                /**
461                 * Returns caller from a certain depth or <code>null</code>
462                 * @param depth how deep in the stack to pull stack frame.
463                 * @return caller or <code>null</code>.
464                 */
465                public static @Nullable Caller ofDepthOrNull(int depth) {
466                        return StackFrameCallerInfo.stackWalker.<@Nullable Caller>walk(
467                                        s -> s.skip(depth + 1).limit(1).map(f -> Caller.of(f)).findFirst().orElse(null));
468                }
469
470                /**
471                 * See {@link StackFrame#getClassName()}.
472                 * @return class name.
473                 */
474                public String className();
475
476                /**
477                 * See {@link StackFrame#getFileName()}.
478                 * @return file name.
479                 */
480                public @Nullable String fileNameOrNull();
481
482                /**
483                 * See {@link StackFrame#getLineNumber()}.
484                 * @return line number.
485                 */
486                public int lineNumber();
487
488                /**
489                 * See {@link StackFrame#getMethodName()}.
490                 * @return method name.
491                 */
492                public String methodName();
493
494                /**
495                 * Make the caller info immutable.
496                 * @return immutable caller info and if this is already immutable return this.
497                 */
498                public Caller freeze();
499
500                /**
501                 * Convenience toString for caller.
502                 * @param caller if caller is <code>null</code> the string "null" will be
503                 * returned.
504                 * @return string representation.
505                 */
506                public static String toString(@Nullable Caller caller) {
507                        /*
508                         * TODO maybe move this to formatters?
509                         */
510                        if (caller == null)
511                                return "null";
512                        return caller.fileNameOrNull() + ":" + caller.lineNumber() + "/" + caller.className() + "."
513                                        + caller.methodName();
514                }
515
516                /**
517                 * Caller info strategies, resolved from
518                 * {@value LogProperties#CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}. {@link #BASIC} is the only
519                 * strategy implemented today (a stack-walk down to the calling
520                 * class/method/line). Using an enum allows additional strategies without changing
521                 * the property format.
522                 */
523                public enum CallerType {
524
525                        /**
526                         * Caller info is not computed.
527                         */
528                        @EnumAlias("false")
529                        NONE,
530                        /**
531                         * Caller info is computed as a single stack frame (class, method, line).
532                         */
533                        @EnumAlias("true")
534                        BASIC;
535
536                        static CallerType parse(String value) {
537                                String v = value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
538                                return switch (v) {
539                                        case "TRUE" -> BASIC;
540                                        case "FALSE" -> NONE;
541                                        default -> LogProperty.enumValue(CallerType.class, value, "true", "false");
542                                };
543                        }
544
545                }
546
547        }
548
549        /**
550         * Rewrites parts of an event for {@link LogEvent#rewrite(LogEvent, Rewriter)}. Each
551         * method is given the original event and by default returns that event's part
552         * unchanged.
553         * <p>
554         * A rewritten event calls the rewriter every time a part is read, so a method may be
555         * called more than once for the same event, and on another thread once the event is
556         * {@linkplain LogEvent#freeze() frozen}. Methods must return the same result for the
557         * same event, and returned key values must not change afterwards.
558         */
559        public interface Rewriter {
560
561                /**
562                 * Appends the message of the rewritten event. The rewritten event has no message
563                 * arguments, so its {@link LogEvent#message()} is this message. Override
564                 * {@link #hasMessage(LogEvent)} too when adding a previously missing message or
565                 * removing an existing one.
566                 * @param event original event.
567                 * @param sb string builder to append to.
568                 * @see LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder)
569                 */
570                default void formattedMessage(LogEvent event, StringBuilder sb) {
571                        event.formattedMessage(sb);
572                }
573
574                /**
575                 * Whether the rewritten event has a message. By default the original event's
576                 * message presence is preserved. Return <code>true</code> when supplying a
577                 * message for an event that had none, or <code>false</code> to remove a message.
578                 * This controls {@link LogEvent#messageOrNull()} and
579                 * {@link LogEvent#formattedMessage(StringBuilder, String)}.
580                 * @param event original event.
581                 * @return whether the rewritten event has a message.
582                 */
583                default boolean hasMessage(LogEvent event) {
584                        return event.hasMessage();
585                }
586
587                /**
588                 * Key values of the rewritten event.
589                 * @param event original event.
590                 * @return key values.
591                 */
592                default KeyValues keyValues(LogEvent event) {
593                        return event.keyValues();
594                }
595
596                /**
597                 * Throwable of the rewritten event.
598                 * @param event original event.
599                 * @return throwable or <code>null</code> for none.
600                 */
601                default @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull(LogEvent event) {
602                        return event.throwableOrNull();
603                }
604
605        }
606
607}
608
609record FrozenCallerInfo(String className, @Nullable String fileNameOrNull, int lineNumber,
610                String methodName) implements LogEvent.Caller {
611        @Override
612        public Caller freeze() {
613                return this;
614        }
615}
616
617record StackFrameCallerInfo(StackFrame stackFrame) implements LogEvent.Caller {
618
619        static final StackWalker stackWalker = StackWalker.getInstance(Option.RETAIN_CLASS_REFERENCE);
620
621        @Override
622        public String className() {
623                return stackFrame.getClassName();
624        }
625
626        @Override
627        public @Nullable String fileNameOrNull() {
628                /*
629                 * TODO checker did not know file name is null.
630                 */
631                return stackFrame.getFileName();
632        }
633
634        @Override
635        public int lineNumber() {
636                return stackFrame.getLineNumber();
637        }
638
639        @Override
640        public String methodName() {
641                return stackFrame.getMethodName();
642        }
643
644        @Override
645        public Caller freeze() {
646                return new FrozenCallerInfo(className(), fileNameOrNull(), lineNumber(), methodName());
647        }
648
649}
650
651record OneArgLogEvent(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level, String loggerName,
652                String message, KeyValues keyValues, LogMessageFormatter messageFormatter, @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull,
653                @Nullable Object arg1) implements LogEvent {
654
655        OneArgLogEvent {
656                Objects.requireNonNull(timestamp, "timestamp");
657                Objects.requireNonNull(threadName, "threadName");
658                Objects.requireNonNull(level, "level");
659                Objects.requireNonNull(loggerName, "loggerName");
660                Objects.requireNonNull(message, "message");
661                Objects.requireNonNull(keyValues, "keyValues");
662                Objects.requireNonNull(messageFormatter, "messageFormatter");
663        }
664
665        @Override
666        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb) {
667                messageFormatter.format(sb, message, arg1);
668        }
669
670        @Override
671        public LogEvent freeze() {
672                return freeze(timestamp);
673        }
674
675        @Override

757/*
758 * An argument-bearing event after formatting. Keeps the unformatted message without
759 * retaining the argument objects, so filters see the same message before and after
760 * freezing.
761 */

763                String message, String formattedMessage, KeyValues keyValues,
764                @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull) implements LogEvent {
765
766        FrozenLogEvent {
767                Objects.requireNonNull(timestamp, "timestamp");
768                Objects.requireNonNull(threadName, "threadName");
769                Objects.requireNonNull(level, "level");
770                Objects.requireNonNull(loggerName, "loggerName");

773                Objects.requireNonNull(keyValues, "keyValues");
774        }
775
776        @Override
777        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb) {
778                sb.append(formattedMessage);
779        }
780
781        @Override
782        public LogEvent freeze() {
783                return this;
784        }
785
786        @Override
787        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp) {
788                return new FrozenLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, message, formattedMessage,
789                                keyValues, throwableOrNull);
790        }
791
792}

794record DefaultLogEvent(Instant timestamp, String threadName, long threadId, System.Logger.Level level,
795                String loggerName, @Nullable String formattedMessage, KeyValues keyValues,
796                @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull) implements LogEvent {
797
798        DefaultLogEvent {
799                Objects.requireNonNull(timestamp, "timestamp");
800                Objects.requireNonNull(threadName, "threadName");
801                Objects.requireNonNull(level, "level");

804        }

807        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb) {
808                sb.append(this.formattedMessage);
809        }

811        @Override
812        public String message() {

814        }

816        @Override

819        }

821        @Override
822        public boolean hasMessage() {

824        }
825
826        @Override
827        public LogEvent freeze() {
828                if (keyValues instanceof MutableKeyValues mkvs) {
829                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, formattedMessage,
830                                        mkvs.freeze(), throwableOrNull);
831                }
832                return this;
833        }

835        @Override
836        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp) {

838                        return new DefaultLogEvent(timestamp, threadName, threadId, level, loggerName, formattedMessage,
839                                        mkvs.freeze(), throwableOrNull);
840                }

842                                throwableOrNull);

847/*
848 * Wraps an event and forwards to it, so a wrapper only overrides what it changes. Every
849 * LogEvent method, defaults included, is forwarded here: a default left to run on the
850 * wrapper would compute from the wrapper instead of the wrapped event.
851 */
852sealed interface ForwardingLogEvent extends LogEvent permits StackFrameLogEvent, LevelLogEvent, RewrittenLogEvent {
853
854        LogEvent event();
855
856        @Override
857        default Instant timestamp() {
858                return event().timestamp();
859        }
860
861        @Override
862        default String threadName() {
863                return event().threadName();
864        }
865
866        @Override
867        default long threadId() {
868                return event().threadId();
869        }
870
871        @Override
872        default Level level() {
873                return event().level();
874        }
875
876        @Override
877        default String loggerName() {
878                return event().loggerName();
879        }
880
881        @Override
882        default String message() {
883                return event().message();
884        }
885
886        @Override
887        default @Nullable String messageOrNull() {
888                return event().messageOrNull();
889        }
890
891        @Override
892        default boolean hasMessage() {
893                return event().hasMessage();
894        }
895
896        @Override
897        default void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb) {
898                event().formattedMessage(sb);
899        }
900
901        @Override
902        default void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb, String fallbackMessage) {
903                event().formattedMessage(sb, fallbackMessage);
904        }
905
906        @Override
907        default @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull() {
908                return event().throwableOrNull();
909        }
910
911        @Override
912        default KeyValues keyValues() {
913                return event().keyValues();
914        }
915
916        @Override
917        default @Nullable Caller callerOrNull() {
918                return event().callerOrNull();
919        }
920
921}
922
923record StackFrameLogEvent(LogEvent event, Caller callerOrNull) implements ForwardingLogEvent {
924
925        StackFrameLogEvent {
926                Objects.requireNonNull(callerOrNull, "caller");
927        }
928
929        @Override
930        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
931        public LogEvent freeze() {
932                var e = event.freeze();
933                var info = callerOrNull.freeze();
934                if (e == event && info == callerOrNull) {
935                        return this;
936                }
937
938                return new StackFrameLogEvent(e, info);
939        }
940
941        @Override
942        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
943        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp) {
944                var e = event.freeze(timestamp);
945                var info = callerOrNull.freeze();
946                if (e == event && info == callerOrNull) {
947                        return this;
948                }
949                return new StackFrameLogEvent(e, info);
950        }
951
952}

954record LevelLogEvent(LogEvent event, Level level) implements ForwardingLogEvent {

956        LevelLogEvent {

959        }
960
961        @Override
962        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
963        public LogEvent freeze() {
964                var e = event.freeze();
965                return e == event ? this : new LevelLogEvent(e, level);
966        }

969        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp) {

971        }
972
973}

975record RewrittenLogEvent(LogEvent event, Rewriter rewriter) implements ForwardingLogEvent {
976
977        RewrittenLogEvent {
978                Objects.requireNonNull(event, "event");
979                Objects.requireNonNull(rewriter, "rewriter");
980        }
981
982        @Override
983        public String message() {
984                var sb = new StringBuilder();
985                formattedMessage(sb);
986                return sb.toString();
987        }
988
989        @Override
990        public boolean hasMessage() {
991                return rewriter.hasMessage(event);
992        }
993
994        @Override
995        public @Nullable String messageOrNull() {
996                return hasMessage() ? message() : null;
997        }
998
999        @Override
1000        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb) {
1001                rewriter.formattedMessage(event, sb);
1002        }
1003
1004        @Override
1005        public void formattedMessage(StringBuilder sb, String fallbackMessage) {
1006                if (hasMessage()) {
1007                        formattedMessage(sb);
1008                }
1009                else {
1010                        sb.append(fallbackMessage);
1011                }
1012        }
1013
1014        @Override
1015        public KeyValues keyValues() {
1016                return rewriter.keyValues(event);
1017        }
1018
1019        @Override
1020        public @Nullable Throwable throwableOrNull() {
1021                return rewriter.throwableOrNull(event);
1022        }
1023
1024        @Override
1025        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality")
1026        public LogEvent freeze() {
1027                var e = event.freeze();
1028                return e == event ? this : new RewrittenLogEvent(e, rewriter);
1029        }
1030
1031        @Override
1032        public LogEvent freeze(Instant timestamp) {
1033                return new RewrittenLogEvent(event.freeze(timestamp), rewriter);
1034        }
1035
1036}
